subject: NovaMed — Post-discovery: Technical deep dive + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novamed.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@novamed.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovaMed — Post-discovery: Technical deep dive + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand NovaMed's goals and the ML/infra constraints. Quick recap from our discovery call: 

- Goal: build an embedding + retrieval layer to power personalized care summaries for clinicians.
- Current model footprint: ensemble of two transformer models (encoder ~350M params, reranker ~200M).
- Traffic profile: peak ~120 req/s, typical request ~800 tokens, expect 50–70% cache hits on session prefixes.
- Success metrics: p95 latency < 200ms for short flows, reasonable tail for long context requests; target cost per 1k requests under project threshold.

Next step: schedule a technical deep dive (60–90 min) with your ML and infra leads to align on architecture, performance targets, data flow, and security (KMS/audit). Proposed agenda below and a couple of time windows — please confirm what works and who will join from your side.

Draft agenda (60–90 min):
1) Introductions and goals (5 min)
2) Current model & infra architecture (15–20 min) — Priya / ML lead
3) Traffic characteristics & SLOs (10–15 min) — Priya / engineering
4) Serving options & tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted vs private) (15–20 min) — Redwood SEs
5) Security / compliance / data handling (10 min)
6) Rollout plan, timeline, and success criteria (10 min)
7) Q&A / next actions (5–10 min)

Suggested attendees from NovaMed: ML lead, Infra/DevOps lead, Security/Compliance, Product Manager. From Redwood: myself, Camila Reyes (Solutions Engineer), and Dylan Brooks (Engineering SE).

Available windows (PDT):
- Wed 3/24: 9:00–11:00 or 14:00–16:00
- Thu 3/25: 10:00–12:00
- Mon 3/29: 13:00–16:00

If none of those fit, share a Calendly link or preferred slots and we’ll match. I’ve attached a short discovery notes PDF and a mutual action plan for reference.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20270322.pdf, mutual-action-plan-novamed.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to coordinating.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198
https://www.redwoodinference.com/

Subject: Re: NovaMed — Post-discovery: Technical deep dive + next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the crisp recap and proposed agenda. That looks good to us. Confirming the attendees from NovaMed: Priya Nair (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra Lead), Emily Chen (Security). Product (Lina Gomez) will try to join but may not be available for the full session.

We can do Thu 3/25 10:00–11:30 PDT — would that work for your team? If you prefer a 60-min slot we can compress the agenda, but given the infra details it may be safer to take 90 minutes.

Also, two asks before the session:
- Can you share a short list of the specific latency/throughput targets you usually design for in similar deployments?
- Any questions we should prepare answers for on our side (e.g., model shard sizes, token distributions, encryption in transit/at rest)?

Appreciate it — Alex

Subject: Re: NovaMed — Post-discovery: Technical deep dive + next steps

Alex / Priya —

Thu 3/25 10:00–11:30 PDT works great — I’ll book the 90-minute slot to make sure we have time for deep discussion. Calendar invite coming shortly.

Quick answers to your asks so the team can prep:
- Typical latency/throughput guidance we design around: p50/p95 targets depend on model size but for similar customer workloads we aim for p95 <= 200–300ms on dedicated pools for common short-context flows; for longer contexts (multi-k tokens) p95 will be higher and we optimize via KV caching and prefix caching to reduce cost/latency. Throughput targets are handled via batching and autoscaling policies — we’ll review batching windows during the call.
- Please prepare: model artifact sizes (weights on disk), average tokens per request (median and 95th), expected concurrency at peak, and any regulatory constraints on where models/data can be hosted.

Draft agenda (attached as tech-deep-dive-agenda.docx) — minor tweak: we’ll add a short section on recommendations from our Optimize team (quantization & batching profiles) toward the end.

I’ve looped in Camila and Dylan who will drive the technical portion from Redwood. Camila will cover serving options and rollout; Dylan will cover runtime optimizations and what we’ll need from your infra/observability side.

Attachments: tech-deep-dive-agenda.docx

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: NovaMed technical deep dive — pre-read and a couple of quick questions

Alex / Priya / team —

Thanks — looking forward to Thu. Quick pre-read attached: a 1-page questionnaire that helps us size the environment and surface obvious integration points ahead of the call (pre-deep-dive-questionnaire.pdf). If you can fill the first two sections before the meeting it will let us prepare targeted performance recommendations.

A couple of quick questions we’ll use during the deep dive:
- What are the approximate max model shard sizes (GB) for your encoder and reranker?
- Expected median tokens per user request vs 95th percentile?
- Any hard p99 SLA requirement we should know about?

We’ll also prepare examples of batching profiles and a reference quantization matrix for encoder/decoder types. If you have an internal runbook or existing monitoring dashboards (Datadog/NewRelic links), please share so we can align on observability hooks.

Attachment: pre-deep-dive-questionnaire.pdf

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
